question: pr3389
answer:
**No runtime regression found.** The diff moves `same_origin`, `is_https_redirect`, and `port_or_default` from `httpx/_utils.py` into `httpx/_client.py` as private helpers. Their logic is unchanged. Five existing redirect-header tests move from `tests/test_utils.py` to `tests/client/test_headers.py` with identical assertions. [Client helpers](httpx/_client.py:61) · [Header tests](tests/client/test_headers.py:240)

**Affected behavior.** `BaseClient._build_redirect_request()` calls `_redirect_headers()` for both `Client` and `AsyncClient`, whether the redirect is followed automatically or exposed as `Response.next_request`. Cross-origin redirects still update `Host` and strip `Authorization`, with an exception for same-host upgrades from HTTP port 80 to HTTPS port 443. The top-level request API and CLI use `Client`, so they inherit the same behavior. [Redirect builder](httpx/_client.py:474) · [Header handling](httpx/_client.py:545) · [Sync loop](httpx/_client.py:976) · [Async loop](httpx/_client.py:1679) · [API](httpx/_api.py:6) · [CLI](httpx/_main.py:17)

**Risks.** Downstream code importing the old names from the private `httpx._utils` module will break. Direct imports of `same_origin` or `is_https_redirect` from `httpx._client` will also break because those names were previously imported there. No other in-repo references were found. The non-default-port test changes both ports together, so it would miss a regression that dropped just one of the two port checks. [Utility module](httpx/_utils.py) · [Port test](tests/client/test_headers.py:284)

The targeted tests could not run because the available Python environment lacks `pytest`.
